A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLHF–DPO study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, references, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original GPT-2-large experiments on PKU-SafeRLHF in Section 5 and numerical bandit simulations in Appendix B.8–B.9.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experiments in Section 5 and numerical simulations in Appendix C.8–C.9.

M1.justification: The RLHF/DPO objectives, online samplers, token-level parameterization, and sparse estimators are retained. The reward-modeling discussion moves from Appendix A to B without changing its proposed procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PKU-SafeRLHF QA, prompt, safer, and better data, the same model-capacity scenarios, and the same bandit simulations. Newly cited applications motivating sparsity are not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: The comparisons remain online DPO versus RLHF/RL for model mis-specification and DPO versus reward modeling for statistical efficiency. The pairwise-regression implementation of RL and the appendix simulation comparators are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 and the implementation appendices retain the same data splits, GPT-2-large-774M models, freezing controls, reward scales, sample-size sweeps, training budgets, and evaluation procedures. The new proofs analyze the existing simulation settings.

E4.justification: The reward-scale, model-capacity, and sample-efficiency analyses are retained, as are both numerical bandit examples. The added analytic proofs strengthen theoretical support without adding an empirical ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions report three seeds in Section 5.1 and display the same shaded uncertainty bands. No new run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: v4 Figures 2–5 match v5 Figures 1–4, including all ten experiment and simulation panels. The curves, rankings, numerical examples, and original empirical findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 Appendix B.8–B.9 explicitly relies on numerical verification of Propositions 4 and 7. v5 Appendix C.8–C.9 adds analytic proofs deriving gradient signs, fixed points, and value inequalities for the same constructions, substantially strengthening the mathematical support for the online-DPO dichotomy.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same model-mis-specification dichotomy, possible online-DPO advantage, and sparsity-based statistical separation. The new proofs support existing central claims rather than redefining them.

C2.justification: v5 adds a sparsity rationale supported by cited examples and explicitly states that the statistical theorems do not directly extend to three or more tokens. It also discusses applicability to other random-utility models and qualifies the single-prompt versus multi-prompt comparison with Nika et al.

D1.justification: v4 Appendix C and v5 Appendix D provide the same code/data access information, preprocessing template, hyperparameters, sampling implementation, hardware, memory requirements, and runtimes.

R1.justification: v5 adds Ackermann et al. on off-policy reward correction and references supporting preference-learning foundations, token-level parameterization, and sparsity/low-rank motivation. It refines the comparison with Nika et al.; the existing broader survey is retained in Appendix A.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes include moving much of related work to Appendix A, adding focused explanatory passages and an Impact Statement, clarifying RLHF terminology, and updating affiliations and conference front matter.

P2.justification: v5 converts the main text and references to a two-column conference layout and replaces v4's Venn-style Figure 1 with a matrix-style Table 1. Existing plots are enlarged and relocated, and appendix layout and equation wrapping change substantially.

improvement.justification: v5 replaces numerical-only support for two central online-DPO propositions with analytic proofs in Appendix C.8–C.9, resolving an important rigor gap in this primarily theoretical paper. The added qualifications about the two-token statistical construction also improve interpretive precision. These gains strengthen the existing contributions while retaining the empirical evidence.
